column2: Ergonomic risk analysis from video and observation: REBA, RULA, the NIOSH lifting equation and other methods in one place, with Excel and PDF reports. No install, no account.
Ergonomic risk analysis from video and observation, method guidance and Excel/PDF reports. Runs in the browser.

The 10 most widely used field methods in one place: REBA, RULA, OWAS, NIOSH, KIM lifting and pushing-pulling (BAuA), Liberty Mutual (Snook), OCRA, ROSA and the Nordic questionnaire. Advanced methods are ready for more specific cases. Every result shows what drives the risk and what can be done.
I don’t know where to start
Find the risky areas with a few yes/no questions; see one recommended method for each area and why.
I have a video or photo
Pick the frame and mark the joints. REBA, RULA and OWAS are calculated together.
I’m in the field, I’ll analyse later
Take photos, grab video frames, mark hazards. Analyse from the list back at your desk.
I have measurements, observations or a survey
NIOSH, KIM lifting and pushing-pulling (BAuA), Liberty Mutual, OCRA, ROSA and Nordic questionnaire forms.

Assess a workstation in four steps. The key questions follow the pre-screening approach of ISO/TR 12295; the environment questions are common field rules.

Structure: Workplace → Station → Task. Analyses are saved to a task; a station’s risk is the worst of the current measurements of its tasks.
Each station × risk area is one row. Values are suggested from the method result; adjust them for your workplace with “Edit”. The table goes into the Excel and PDF reports as is.

contains a summary, results and a separate sheet per method; download a task’s own report from its heading and a single record’s assessment form from its card. The CSV is in long format (one method result per row) and goes straight into an Excel or Power BI pivot. JSON is a full backup.
Excel download is not available in this view; use Copy CSV instead.
Plan an action → implement it → measure the same task again. When the re-measurement is saved, the before-after comparison appears here and on the station page.
Acceptable if the posture is not held or repeated for long.
Further investigation needed, change may be needed.
Corrective action needed in the near future.
Corrective action needed as soon as possible.
Bring the work point between waist and shoulder: lift table, pallet raiser, tilted bin. Reduce picks from the floor.
Set the working height relative to elbow level; bring the material closer to the body.
Move pick and place points in front of the worker; leave room to turn with the feet instead of the trunk.
Bring the screen, display or workpiece closer to eye level; improve lighting and reading distance.
Shorten the reach and lower the work point; place frequently used parts within arm’s length.
Lower the work surface or raise the worker with a platform/step.
Use a bent-handle tool, put the workpiece on a rotating fixture; lay out the work so the wrist stays straight.
Raise work that requires squatting; provide a firm, level floor and knee pads/sitting support if needed.
Split the load, use a mechanical aid (vacuum lifter, pallet truck, balance arm); use a two-person lift if needed.
Switch to crates and boxes with handholds; add handles to slippery surfaces.
Plan job rotation and short micro-breaks; reduce long holding with a fixture or support.
Rearrange the flow, remove steps that require sudden movements; check floor stability.
Seat height adjustable; feet flat on the floor (or a footrest is provided)
Set the chair so the knees are level with the hips; provide a footrest if the feet do not reach the floor.
Seat depth suitable: 2–3 fingers’ gap between the back of the knee and the seat edge
Use a chair with depth adjustment or shorten the depth with a lumbar cushion.
Lumbar support present and in line with the small of the back
Adjust the lumbar support height or add a separate lumbar cushion.
Armrests do not lift the shoulders; elbows comfortably supported
Lower or remove the armrests; bring them level with the desk.
Top edge of the screen at or slightly below eye level
Adjust the screen with a monitor arm/riser. On a laptop use a riser + external keyboard/mouse.
Screen about an arm’s length away (50–75 cm)
Move the screen to where your fingertips touch it with an outstretched arm; enlarge the text.
Screen straight ahead, neck not turned
Put the main screen straight ahead; with two screens, centre the one used most.
No reflections or glare on the screen, documents at screen level
Place the screen at right angles to the window and use a document holder.
